requirements.requirement: Create the datauser account on node1
requirements.summary: adduser -D created datauser (uid 1001, gid 1001), confirmed via id command output.

requirements.requirement: Limit datauser to 100MB of storage under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem itself
requirements.summary: A dedicated ext4 loopback filesystem was mounted at /srv/data with native ext4 quota feature enabled (tune2fs -O quota), and setquota applied a 102400 1K-block (100MB) soft=hard user quota for datauser via the kernel quota subsystem, not application-level checks.

requirements.requirement: Enforcement verified: writes beyond 100MB fail, writes within limit succeed
requirements.summary: A 150MB write as datauser was halted by the kernel at ~99MB with 'Quota exceeded' (EDQUOT); a subsequent 50MB write succeeded, directly demonstrating filesystem-level enforcement rather than a config-only claim.

requirements.requirement: Quota configuration persists across reboot (fstab + boot-time quotaon)
requirements.summary: fstab entry with usrquota,grpquota added; /etc/local.d/srv-data-quota.start created and 'local' runlevel service enabled. A full restart cycle was captured: pre-restart baseline (boot_id 412576a1..., mount, quota state, marker file) followed by a reboot, a changed boot_id (11f48b77...) confirming the reboot occurred, and post-restart verification showing /srv/data auto-remounted with quota options, quota accounting on, the same 100MB limit in repquota, the marker file intact, and a repeat over-quota write test again failing with 'Quota exceeded'.

overall_summary: The task's material outcomes are all directly and coherently satisfied: datauser was created, a filesystem-enforced (native ext4 quota) 100MB limit was applied to /srv/data for datauser, enforcement was verified with over- and under-limit writes, and the quota configuration was shown to persist through a full observed reboot cycle (changed boot identity plus recovered mount, quota, and data state). The provider-wide restart-evidence protocol was satisfied with a coherent pre/post boot-identity transition matching the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good with only minor uncleaned log files in /tmp.
limitations: Only a single restart cycle for node1 was captured; no additional stress (e.g., inode limits, group quota behavior) was tested beyond block quota enforcement, though this matches the task's stated scope (storage/byte limit).

The initial deprecated-quota-file attempt (cmd-572b90fdf4484db4) failed partway through and left an intermediate state that was corrected in the next command; this is noted as a minor troubleshooting step rather than a deficiency.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were almost entirely purposeful: package install, account creation, filesystem/quota setup, enforcement tests, persistence configuration, and the mandatory restart-evidence cycle. An initial attempt used the deprecated ext4 external quota-file approach (cmd-572b90fdf4484db4, exit 1) and was immediately corrected by switching to the native ext4 quota feature via tune2fs (cmd-821c04fdd5794d9e), a reasonable in-line self-correction rather than an unnecessary mutation. cmd-312d46f45a574bfb largely duplicates enforcement tests already performed and exited non-zero, but caused no lasting state change. The only residue is three log files left in /tmp (apkupdate.log, apkadd.log, reboot.log) visible in the after_executor snapshot diff, which are low-risk, bounded artifacts from routine package install/reboot operations and were not cleaned up.
